title: A wall that makes its own joints.
subtitle: What if the neighboring stones were part of the mold?
summary: A workable mass settles between irregular neighbors. Timber and cloth support the exposed face as the new block takes the shape of its surroundings.
sceneDescription: A polygonal wall with one warm-colored block deforming into the space between its neighbors, behind a removable cloth and timber support.
modelNote: The fit is prescribed by geometry. This animation does not simulate putty mechanics, prove a recipe, or reproduce a surveyed Cusco wall.

steps.name: Support
steps.title: Give the face something to rest against.
steps.text: A timber frame and a cloth facing hold the proposed workable material at the front. Existing stones define the other boundaries.

steps.name: Place
steps.title: Bring in a yielding mass.
steps.text: This scenario starts with a thick, putty-like mixture. Its behavior would differ from a freely poured liquid or a rigid H-block mold.

steps.name: Press
steps.title: Let the neighbors define the joint.
steps.text: The illustrated mass deforms into the irregular gap. A very close fit follows from using the adjacent surfaces as boundaries.

steps.name: Set
steps.title: Keep the shape as it hardens.
steps.text: The critical material question is whether a real mixture can set with sufficiently little shrinkage, slump, or adhesion to its neighbors.

steps.name: Uncover
steps.title: Remove the support. Keep the fit.
steps.text: The facing moves away to reveal the joint. A physical trial could also test whether cloth weave or support pressure leaves recognizable marks.

issues.title: Close-fitting, irregular joints
issues.mechanism: A workable block can take an impression of neighboring surfaces instead of being repeatedly lifted for fitting.
issues.remaining: Shrinkage and release still matter. Separate, tight-fitting blocks must remain separate after curing.

issues.title: Putting a block into a confined gap
issues.mechanism: Material can arrive in small batches and acquire its final shape inside the wall.
issues.remaining: This changes the size of each load, not the total mass to deliver or the need for access and support.

hypothesis: This is a candidate construction sequence inspired by the broader cast-stone proposal. The cloth arrangement and deformation are illustrative design choices, not recovered Inca equipment.
alternative: Careful dressing, trial fitting, and abrasion provide a conventional account of polygonal masonry. A close joint by itself does not discriminate between these processes.
test: Build a small wall using a specified putty-like mixture. Measure slump, joint gaps before and after curing, bonding between blocks, and marks from the facing. Compare against a dressed-stone control.
